correctness.rationale: The Gaussian holomorphic monomials are orthogonal to the nonconstant antiholomorphic monomials, so the two kernels are exp(z·conj(w)/α) and its sum with its conjugate minus 1. With evaluation weighted by e^(−t/2)√m_±, T=E*E shares its nonzero spectrum with EE*. The normalized two-by-two matrices have identical diagonal (m_+,m_−); their off-diagonals divided by √(m_+m_−) are respectively u² and q/D, q=u(2u−1), D=2−u. Both have rank two: 1−u⁴>0 and (D−q)(D+q)=4(1−u²)(1−u+u²)>0. At fixed diagonal the upper eigenvalue [m_++m_−+√((m_+−m_−)²+4m_+m_−c²)]/2 is strictly increasing in |c|, independently of the two positive masses. When u≥1/2, q≥0 and u²>q/D is equivalent to 1>u². When u<1/2, |q|/D>u² exactly when 1−4u+u²>0. This changes sign only at u=2−√3 in that interval. Since u falls as t rises, the claimed majorizations follow. At equality q/D=−u², sign conjugation gives equality of the whole spectrum. This also covers repeated positive eigenvalues when the pluriharmonic off-diagonal vanishes and the masses are equal. Convex/concave x^p gives the strict p>1 and 0<p<1 directions; p=1 is always equal after normalization; p=∞ follows from the top eigenvalue. At a=0 both masses merge with D=1. This direct symbolic comparison is a full replay of the result; the frozen numerical diagnostic was inspected, not executed, and is not needed for any quantifier.

evidence: With the same diagonal the result is equivalent to crossing of absolute normalized kernel correlations u² and |u(2u−1)|/(2−u), not just to a Schatten inequality at one p.

Equal absolute correlations can instead occur when the pluriharmonic correlation is negative; that is the claimed threshold. value.rationale: Two positive masses form the first rank at which trace-normalized spectral order can differ at all; at rank one trace equality fixes the spectrum. The antipodal geometry, a natural symmetric test for the two kernel types, has a strict and sharp reversal, rather than a universal ordering suggested by a one-atom norm ratio. The exact boundary is useful for testing spectral comparisons simultaneously across all positive mass ratios and convex or concave power sums.
